info.title: Link Money API

tags.name: Client Management
tags.description:
There are three kinds of people who interact with Link Money: 
- **Users** are the people who use the Link Money application. They are the people who log in, view their accounts, and make transactions.
- **Clients** are the people who use the Link Money API. They are the people who build applications that interact with the Link Money API.
- **Tenants** are the organizations that use Link Money. They are the people who manage the users and clients who interact with Link Money. Generally speaking, the `user` is an end user of the `tenant`'s application, and the `client` is a developer who is building the `tenant`'s application. 

Every developer must have a client configuration in order to access Link Money. This includes developers who are operating within a tenant environment that they themselves manage. 

## Webhooks 
Link Money supports all available Yodlee webhooks, which are documented in the [Yodlee API documentation](https://developer.envestnet.com/resources/yodlee/webhooks/docs). Developers can subscribe to webhooks by sending requests to the Link Money API webhook management endpoints. 

As each Link Money tenant is a separate environment, each tenant requires its own webhook subscription. Make sure you authenticate with a token that has the proper tenant ID to ensure tha the webhook subscription is created in the correct tenant environment.

Link Money tenants are shared by multiple clients, so it is possible to receive webhook notifications from customers who are not specifically accessing your application. Make sure that your application logic accounts for events that are related to users who other clients may have registered.

tags.name: Fastlink

id.description: A UUID unique identifier for the webhook.

uri.description: The URI address where the webhook is meant to go.

webhookTypes.description: An array of the webhook types that your URI is registered to receive.

items.description: The type of webhook you want sent to this URI.

webhookDisabled.description: A boolean indicating whether the webhook is disabled.

status.description: An enumerator indicating the health status of the webhook; can be null, 'HEALTHY', or 'UNHEALTHY'.

lastAttempt.description: A timestamp of the last time a webhook was attempted. Can be null if no attempt has been made.

lastAttemptStatus.description: The HTTP response code received at the last attempt. Can be null if no attempt has been made.

lastSuccess.description: A timestamp of the last time a webhook was successfully sent (received a 2XX response). Can be null if no successful attempt has been made.

clientDescription.example: A budgeting tool for a hardy folk.

registrationDate.description: The date your client was registered.

webhookIds.description: A list of webhook IDs associated with your client.

tenants.description: A list of tenant IDs that your client is allowed to access.

name.description: The name of the tenant for easy identification.

tenantId.description: The unique identifier for the tenant.

clients.description: A list of client IDs that have access to the tenant environment.

scopes.tenantId: Varies according to the tenant you are trying to access.

post.description:
Obtain an access token using client credentials. The request must include `clientId`, `clientSecret`, and the custom claims `tenantId` and `userId` to specify the tenant and end user the token will represent.
`tenantId` is only required in cases where you are trying to access a tenant-specific resource. Some routes, like those that let you view and alter your client configuration, do not require a token with this claim. `userId` is only required in cases where you are trying to access a user-specific _and_ tenant-specific resource. Some routes, like those that let you generate new users, do not require a token with this claim, even if they do require a token with a tenant claim.

tenantId.description: The ID of the tenant the developer wishes to access.

userId.description: The ID of the end user the developer is acting on behalf of.

200.description: A JSON object containing the access token.

scope.description: The scope(s) for which the token is valid, corresponding to the institution ID.

items.example: Expected 'webhookUrl' to be a string, but received 'null' instead.

documentation.description: A link to the documentation for this error.

received.description: The JSON of the payload that we received from you.

expected.description: The expected formatting for the JSON the endpoint requires. This varies from endpoint to endpoint.

401.description:
Unauthorized. The oauth token call can return Unauthorized for the following reasons: 
  - Your client ID is invalid. 
  - Your client secret is invalid. 
  - Your tenant ID is invalid. 
  - Your client is not authorized to access the specified tenant. 

The `details` field in the response body will provide the specific reason why your authentication failed.

get.description: This endpoint returns details about your client's current configuration.

details.example: The client endpoint requires a valid access token. Either none was provided, or the token provided was invalid. Please check your client credentials and try again.

get.summary: View a list of your currently-configured webhooks.
get.description:
This endpoint returns the full list of webhooks currently configured for your client. 

The list has a default length of 10 items. For additional webhooks, use the `limit` and `offset` parameters to paginate the query.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of webhooks to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of webhooks to skip before returning results.

post.description: Allows clients to create a new webhook configuration by specifying the URI. The system generates all other fields.

uri.description: The HTTPS URI where the webhook will be sent. Must be a valid HTTPS URL.

webhookTypes.description: The types of webhooks that you want sent to the specified URI.

items.description: The type of webhook you want sent to this URI.

webhookDisabled.description: A boolean indicating whether the webhook is disabled.

get.description: Fetches the details of a specific webhook configuration using its unique identifier.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The UUID of the webhook to retrieve.

404.description: Webhook with specified ID not found.

patch.description:
Use the update webhook endpoint to change details of one of your webhook configurations. Using this endpoint, you can: 
  - Change the URI where the webhook sends data.
  - Update the types of webhooks you receive.
  - Temporarily disable the webhook.
  - Re-enable a disabled webhook.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the webhook to update.

uri.description: The new URI where the webhook will send data.

webhookTypes.description: The types of webhooks the developer wishes to receive.

webhookDisabled.description: Flag to disable the webhook temporarily.

400.description: Invalid input, e.g., invalid URI format or invalid enum value for webhookTypes.

404.description: Webhook with specified ID not found.

delete.description: Deletes a specific webhook configuration and returns the deleted webhook's data.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the webhook to delete.

200.description: Webhook configuration deleted successfully. Returns the original webhook data.

404.description: Webhook with specified ID not found.

post.description: Allows developers to trigger a test webhook event. This sends a dummy payload to the configured URI of the webhook identified by {webhookId}. This helps in verifying the webhook setup.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the webhook to test.

200.description: Webhook test initiated and response received.

receivedResponse.description: Whether a response was received from the webhook endpoint.

responseCode.description: The HTTP response code received from the webhook endpoint. Null if no response was received.

firedAt.description: The timestamp when the webhook payload was fired.

receivedAt.description: The timestamp when the response from the webhook was received. Null if no response was received.

processingDuration.description: The duration in seconds it took for the webhook to process the request. Calculated as the difference between receivedAt and firedAt. Null if no response was received.

post.description: Provides necessary details for developers to integrate FastLink4 into their applications without exposing sensitive credentials. Requires user-level authentication.

loginName.description: The ID of the user for whom the Fastlink 4 session belongs. This can be any string of your choosing, although it is best to associate it with the unique identifier in your own system that most corresponds to one actual individual person.

accessToken.description: The user token for the FastLink4 frontend.

fastLinkURL.description: The tenant-specific URL to embed FastLink4 as an iframe.

401.description: Unauthorized. The user or tenant details are incorrect or do not have the necessary permissions.

403.description: Forbidden. Access is denied due to invalid credentials or access rights.
